transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, hey Doc. I, uh, I guess I'm here because... well, honestly, I just can't take it anymore. It's like... I feel like I got a motor running inside me all day long. Just this engine that won't shut off, you know? And if I have to sit still—man, it's the absolute worst. 

Like, I try to go to church, right? I want to just sit in the pew and listen to the sermon, but I can't. I feel completely trapped. My whole body just screams at me that I have to get up or do something. I end up having to walk out to the back or pace around because sitting there feels impossible, like I'm gonna explode if I don't move. And it ain't just church, it's everywhere. Even out in your waiting room at the clinic just now, I felt like the walls were closing in on me just because I was supposed to wait in a chair. I was up and down, looking out the window, shifting around. Same exact thing happens at home. I can't just sit on the couch and watch a show. I feel stuck, like I'm tied down, and I just have to get up and move or mess with something. It's just this constant, revving feeling, from the minute I wake up, and I can't ever just be still.
Have you recently started or changed the dose of any medications, especially antipsychotic or anti-nausea drugs, around the time these restless feelings began?

No, no sir. I ain't taking nothing like that. I mean, I don't even really go to the doctor much to be getting any prescriptions in the first place, you know? Like, my mom used to try and get me to take stuff for headaches or whatever back in the day, but I just never liked messing with pills. So, no anti... what did you call it? Antipsychotic? Nah, definitely nothing like that. And my stomach's been fine, so no anti-nausea stuff either. 

I think the last time I took anything for my stomach was maybe, shoot, five or six years ago when I ate some bad gas station food, but that was just Pepto, you know? Just the regular pink stuff you buy at the store. But lately? No, not a single thing. And honestly, doc, this feeling... it didn't just start up out of nowhere like some bad reaction to a pill. It's not like I swallowed something last week and suddenly my legs wouldn't stop bouncing. It's just... it's just always there, you know? It's like I'm wired up, but it definitely ain't from no medicine. I don't even have a regular doctor to prescribe me anything anyway, which is why I finally came in here today, 'cause I just can't keep living with this motor running all the time. So yeah, no new meds, no old meds, just... just me.
Along with this restless, 'motor running' feeling, have you also noticed your mood being unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, or your thoughts racing, especially over the past week or two?

Elevated? Euphoric? I ain't even sure I know exactly what euphoric means, to be honest with you, doc. Like, super happy or something? No, definitely not that. I mean, how in the world could I be super happy when I'm constantly having to get up and pace a hole in my living room rug? It's just exhausting, really. So no, I ain't walking around on cloud nine or feeling on top of the world or nothing like that. 

And I wouldn't say I'm unusually irritable either. I mean, sure, I get a little ticked off sometimes, like if I drop a wrench or if I stub my toe, but who doesn't, right? But it ain't like I'm snapping at people for no reason over the past couple weeks. Nothing's changed lately. It's exactly the same as it was a month ago, or a year ago, or five years ago. 

As for my thoughts racing... well, I mean, my brain is always a little noisy, I guess. Kinda like a TV left on in the other room, just a constant hum of stuff. But they ain't racing like I'm going crazy or coming up with wild ideas. Just jumping around a bit, exactly like they always do. Like, since I ain't working a regular job right now, I got a lot of time to just mess around the house, right? So I'll be out in the yard, and I'll start picking up sticks, and then I'll see a weird bug and watch that for a second, and then I'll wonder if the mail came, and then I'll go check the mailbox, and then I'll forget I was picking up sticks. But that ain't some new thing that just started a week or two ago. That's just my normal everyday life. It's always been like that. So no, no weird new moods or super fast thoughts. Just this same old physical motor running in my body that just won't quit.

Thinking back to when you were a kid, in grade school say, did you have that same kind of restless, can't-sit-still feeling back then, or is this something that's only been part of your life as an adult?

Oh man, grade school? Let me tell you, it was exactly the same back then, maybe even worse because they actually expected you to sit at a tiny little desk for hours on end. I swear, every single teacher I ever had must have hated me. They were always, and I mean *always*, moving my seat. It was like a game of musical chairs, but I was the only one playing and I was always losing. First I’d be in the front row so they could keep an eye on me, but then I’d be tapping my foot or rocking my chair, and they’d move me to the back. Then in the back, I’d be messing with the blinds or tapping my pencil on the radiator, so they’d move me to the side of the room. It just never ended. 

I just could not stay put, doc. It was like that motor I was telling you about was already fully installed and running on high gear even back when I was eight years old. I remember this one teacher, Mrs. Gable, third grade—she actually taped a square on the floor around my desk with that thick red duct tape and told me if I stepped outside the square, I was getting a detention. And you know what? I got a detention almost every single day because I just couldn't help it. I’d be sitting there, and suddenly my legs would just push me up, and I’d be standing. 

And it wasn't just the sitting, either. I talked out of turn constantly. If something popped into my head, it just came right out of my mouth before I even realized I was opening it. I’d just blurt out the answer, or ask a question about something completely different, or just make a noise. And getting in trouble for jumping up before class was done? Oh yeah, that was my signature move. The second I thought we were close to the bell, or if I finished a worksheet early, I was up and heading for the door. I’d be halfway down the hall before the teacher even finished saying "class dismissed." So yeah, to answer your question, this ain't nothing new. It’s been my whole life, as far back as I can remember. Just a constant, never-ending struggle to keep myself in one spot.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a lifelong, pervasive pattern of motor restlessness ('motor running'), inability to remain seated in multiple settings (church, waiting room, home), impulsive blurting out of answers/interrupting, and leaving seat before tasks/activities are finished. These hyperactive-impulsive symptoms began in childhood (documented as early as age 8, third grade) and have persisted unchanged into adulthood, causing functional impairment across settings (school, home, social/religious settings). Some inattentive symptoms (distractibility, forgetting tasks midway, jumping from one activity to another) are also present, supporting a combined presentation. Akathisia was ruled out by absence of antipsychotic/antiemetic exposure and the chronic, non-episodic nature of symptoms. Mania/hypomania was ruled out by explicit denial of elevated/irritable mood, euphoria, or true racing thoughts, and by the longstanding, non-episodic course. The combination of childhood onset, cross-situational impairment, and both hyperactive-impulsive and inattentive symptoms supports ADHD, combined presentation.
